articles.title: Rishabh Pant or Ishan Kishan: Who should be Team India's backup wicket-keeper for the 2027 ODI World Cup
articles.description: The ICC Cricket World Cup 2027 is just a year away from now. Teams have started preparing for the mega event. The tournament is all set to be played between October 02 and November 21, 2027, and will be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. The 14th edition will feature 14 teams, where Australia will defend their title. The tournament will follow the preliminary stage, group stage, Super 7, and knockout stage format. Team India, along with Australia, New Zealand, England, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh, have made it through the ranking system. South Africa and Zimbabwe have qualified as co-hosts, while Namibia, who are the third hosts of the tournament, will play the qualifier round. Team India will enter the tournament as one of the strongest contenders to lift the championship. They came very close in the last edition at home, but they lost the final against Australia in Ahmedabad. India have won two World Cup titles (1983 and 2011) and are eyeing their third World Cup championship. 2027 ODI World Cup: Best possible combination for India Team India are currently the no. 1 ranked ODI team in the world. Under the captaincy of Shubman Gill, India will possess an experienced side for the mega event. The top order with Rohit Sharma, Gill, and Virat Kohli is pretty much shorted. India have Shreyas Iyer and KL Rahul in the middle order, while Hardik Pandya (if fit) and Axar Patel are all-rounders. There are plenty of bowling options for India, including Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Kuldeep Yadav, Varun Chakravarthy, and others. However, it will be a long tournament, and with only 15-17 players to pick in the squad, India need some good backup options. Especially, with the gloves. Rahul is currently the first-choice wicket-taker in this format, and India will be looking a good backup keeper among the current lot. 2027 ODI World Cup: Rishabh Pant or Ishan Kishan as backup keeper There will be a tussle between Pant and Ishan for the place as the backup keeper for the 2027 ODI World Cup. These two left-handers have been playing in the ODI team whenever Rahul is not available. After Rahul, these two are currently the most experienced keepers in the Indian ODI setup. Kishan currently holds the edge over Pant in the ODIs. He has been a key part of the T20I setup, and India have kept him in ODIs whenever they have had a chance. Speaking of Pant, India have looked at him more as a test specialist as of now. That is why he hasn't featured in the white-ball game for India since 2024. His last ODI was in August 2024. Pant is a proven match-winner in the longest format, but he hasn't been able to deliver consistently in the white-ball format as he would have liked. 2027 ODI World Cup: Rishabh Pant or Ishan Kishan (Our pick) There is no doubt about the ability of two left-handers with the bat. These two are among the fiercest Indian batters in the current setup and have delivered match-winning performances at the highest level. However, Ishan is clearly ahead of Pant in the race for the 2027 ODI World Cup. There are a few reasons behind it. Not just with the gloves, Ishan also gives a backup option at the top for India. If needed, he can open or bat at no. 3 or 4. On the other hand, Pant is more of a middle-order batter in this format. Secondly, Pant's ODI record hasn't been impressive. He has played 31 ODIs and scored 871 runs at a below-par average of 33.50 with one century and five half-centuries. Ishan has played 32 ODIs and has scored 1107 runs at 42.57 with two centuries and seven half-centuries. He has also scored a double century in this format. The stats and numbers are also backing Ishan over Pant. His inclusion also gives India more flexibility with the bat, as he has also given some important knocks in the middle order. Both batters come with x-factors and striking ability. However, with the current Indian management, Ishan seems to have an edge for the spot as the backup wicket-keeper.
